parallel.requirements: Parallel saw the same three requirements: cpachecker_v0 value analysis, cpachecker_v1 predicate analysis, and cpachecker_v3 k-induction/BMC for 12 benchmark checks.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It created task records for all three stages, implemented v0 itself, and then launched a v0 adversarial audit Workflow while intending to build v1 in the parent.
parallel.implementation: The durable implementation was cpachecker_v0. The parent began symbolic and predicate-analysis files, but predicateAnalysis hung on nondet_safe and no v1 or v3 requirement patch was committed.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Official collection found only one requirement patch, cpachecker_v0.diff, matching the final git log with only the v0 implementation commit beyond the initial state.
parallel.verification: Local v0 checks passed and a full run.sh checkpoint showed 4 of 12 correct. Later predicateAnalysis timed out, and official pytest saw run.sh exceed 300 seconds before v0 result extraction finished.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: v1 remained unfinished/hanging, v3 was not completed, workflow audit output did not become a useful delivered result, and the official solution failed with v0 errors from run.sh timeout.

serial.requirements: Serial received the same three-stage task and requirement list, with progress updates moving from v0 remaining state to v1/v3 and finally v3 only.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor owned each stage in order: v0 in round one, v1 in round two, and initial v3 work in round three with workflows and delegation disabled.
serial.implementation: Serial implemented and committed v0, then implemented v1 using internal linear arithmetic, loop helpers, predicate analysis, symbolic expressions, and v1 tests.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The final serial artifact contained two requirement patches, cpachecker_v0.diff and cpachecker_v1.diff; v3 was not committed before the rate-limit ending.
serial.verification: Serial ran 39 local tests covering v0 and v1 successfully, and official post-test output passed all v0 and v1 cases before failing the four v3 value checks.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Serial failed overall because cpachecker_v3 remained unimplemented or incorrect, producing zeroes for k-induction and BMC acceptance signals.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run received the full three-stage CPAchecker task and recognized v0, v1, and v3 as required, with all 12 benchmark checks in scope.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run received the same prompt and requirement coverage state, and subsequent rounds showed the same remaining requirement slugs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no material requirements misunderstanding; the difference is that parallel delivered only v0, while serial later delivered v1 as well before both failed v3.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel created task entries for v0, v1, and v3, then after v0 launched an auxiliary v0 audit workflow while the parent continued toward v1.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial proceeded by rounds: v0 was already present, round two owned v1 directly, and round three started the remaining v3 work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel diverted parallel capacity into validating the already-passing v0 stage, while serial allocated its next work unit directly to the next unmet stage, v1.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel evidence shows no concrete missing child requirement or cross-agent interface contract; the audit workflow was scoped to v0 rather than producing interoperating implementation pieces.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run kept requirements and implementation state within one actor and reused the v0 foundation when implementing v1.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Context transfer is not the explanatory boundary; serial's advantage came from sequential continuity rather than from better handoff content.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented and committed cpachecker_v0, then started symbolic and predicate-analysis code but left v1 unresolved and v3 unimplemented.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial committed cpachecker_v0 and cpachecker_v1; v1 added linear arithmetic, loop helpers, predicate analysis, symbolic expressions, and tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial's implementation path advanced one full requirement farther. Parallel's final committed artifact remained v0-only despite substantial uncommitted v1 attempts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel workflow generated child logs and was not retrieved without stop; its audit result did not become a useful whole-task checkpoint, and v1 never reached a committed result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial converted completed v1 work into a requirement patch and commit before starting v3.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's auxiliary workflow lifecycle ended as unretrieved audit state, while serial's main implementation lifecycle produced a durable v1 patch.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel official collection found only one requirement patch, matching the v0-only git history; no write collision or overwrite is evidenced.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial official collection found two requirement patches, matching v0 and v1 commits, with no delegation or shared-state collision.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The integration difference is delivered coverage rather than shared-state corruption: serial had v0+v1 patches, parallel only v0.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel locally saw value analysis pass and full run.sh at 4/12, but predicateAnalysis then timed out and official v0 pytest setup timed out running the whole script.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial locally passed 39 v0/v1 tests, and official post-test output shows v0 and v1 test groups passing before v3 failures.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial reached evaluator-aligned acceptance for v0 and v1; parallel did not preserve evaluator-completable behavior because unfinished v1 made run.sh exceed the fixture timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent a large budget with one workflow call, 24 workflow child logs, and later parent-local v1 debugging before ending with only v0 collected.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no delegation, carried state across three serial rounds, committed two requirements, and then stopped with v3 incomplete under the final API limit.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's auxiliary fan-out consumed scarce run budget before indispensable v1/v3 completion; serial spent the comparable control budget directly on the staged implementation path.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official relation is both_fail from current status.json evaluation, but the failure shapes differ sharply. Parallel delivered only v0 and its final run.sh timed out inside unfinished later analysis, causing even v0 official tests to error. Serial delivered v0 and v1 patches; official v0 and v1 tests passed, and only the v3 k-induction/BMC checks failed. The concrete task-solving difference is therefore one completed stage versus two completed stages, driven in parallel by a v0 audit fan-out and unfinished v1/v3 path, while serial kept advancing through unmet requirements.
parallel_contributors: Launched a broad v0 adversarial audit workflow after v0 was already locally passing while v1 and v3 remained necessary.
Hit a predicateAnalysis timeout on nondet_safe and ended with only cpachecker_v0.diff collected.
Final official run.sh exceeded the v0 test fixture timeout, so v0 official checks were reported as errors rather than passes.
serial_contributors: Committed both cpachecker_v0.diff and cpachecker_v1.diff before beginning v3.
Validated v1 with 39 local tests and official v0/v1 cases passed before v3 failures.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial's v3 implementation was absent or inadequate, producing four v3 official failures.
Parallel's predicate solver/analysis attempt had an ordinary performance/correctness defect on nondet_safe in addition to the coordination budget problem.
evaluator_effects: Parallel v0 official errors came from the v0 pytest fixture running the whole run.sh and timing out after 300 seconds, not from evidence that the value-analysis outputs themselves were wrong.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributor to worse parallel task coverage, not an official pass/fail differential because both modes failed

candidates.reason: Reject: the parallel parent explicitly created implementation tasks for v0, v1, and v3 and personally implemented v0 and attempted v1; the failure was not absence of an implementer.
Reject: there were no separately completed component implementations needing an unassigned reconciler; the parent owned code changes and integration.
Reject: the missing deliverables were unfinished requirements, not completed components lacking a final packaging owner.
Reject: the parent handled planning, commits, patches, and tests; the pipeline problem was budget consumed before later stages, not an ownerless pipeline.
Reject: productive v0 implementation started immediately and the later workflow was an audit, not a mandatory serial preflight blocking all work.
Reject: the v0 audit ran in the background while the parent attempted v1 rather than forming a completed serial investigation phase before implementation.
Reject: this is the nearest allocation neighbor, but the directly evidenced event is collective v0 audit fan-out and budget exhaustion, making Fan-out Budget Exhaustion more specific.

After local v0 success and a full-suite checkpoint still showing only 4 of 12 benchmarks correct, the parallel parent launched a broad adversarial Workflow focused on v0 while v1 and v3 were still required. The status record shows 24 workflow child logs from that fan-out, and the parent then hit a predicateAnalysis timeout on nondet_safe. The official artifact collected only cpachecker_v0.diff and the final run.sh timed out under the incomplete later analysis, so even the v0 pytest fixture errored. Serial used the next round for v1, got all 39 local v0/v1 tests passing, committed cpachecker_v1.diff, and official v0/v1 tests passed. This is a realized parallel-side fan-out budget exhaustion episode that explains worse task coverage, not a pass/fail outcome differential because both modes failed.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parallel run closed with only the v0 requirement patch, an unfinished/hanging predicate-analysis path, no v3 implementation, and official v0 tests errored because run.sh exceeded the 300 second fixture timeout.
candidates.near_match_reason: Critical-Path Starvation is a plausible downstream description, but the concrete boundary is the collective v0 audit Workflow breadth plus budget exhaustion before v1/v3 closure.
